title: Saphorackam
summary: Saphorackam is recorded as a locality in southern Brooklyn, near the Long Island strand of the North River bay.
history_content: The name appears in a November 28, 1639 patent from Governor Willem Kieft to Thomas Bescher, a tobacco planter, for land near Saphorakam.
translation_content:
Saphorackam is interpreted as likely meaning "tobacco plantation," connecting the name with words for tobacco and cultivated or broken-up land.

Why Place Names Matter

“City names are more than labels on maps; they are compact records of who lived somewhere, what language they spoke, and what they valued.”

— ICN editorial team, How Cities Get Their Names (2026), ‘Why city names matter’
preservation_content: Saphorackam links Brooklyn's early colonial waterfront records to Native-language place naming and to the cultivation of tobacco in the seventeenth century.
